name: Coloretto: Secret Favourites
summary: Three players take turns placing face-up cards into three rows or taking a row. Over three cycles they collect colours, scored against a secret Favourite colour that each player sees only for themselves.

setup: Fill the deck with 38 cards: 7 each of Red, Blue, Green, Yellow and Purple, and 3 '+2'.
Draw one card at random from deck into top_card and remove it from deck.
Set row_1, row_2, row_3 and closed_rows to empty lists.
Set every player's red, blue, green, yellow, purple and plus2 to 0, and taken to false.

For each player, draw one colour at random from favourite_pool into that player's favourite and remove it from favourite_pool, so the Favourites all differ. Each favourite is visible only to its owner, and the 2 left in favourite_pool are never shown.
Sync each player their own state.

round.effect: Announce row_1, row_2, row_3, closed_rows, top_card, every player's red/blue/green/yellow/purple/plus2, every player's taken, cycle and active_seat.

round.answer: one of place_1, place_2, place_3, take_1, take_2, take_3, limited to the legal ones: place_k only if k is not in closed_rows and len(row_k) < 3; take_k only if k is not in closed_rows and len(row_k) >= 1

round.effect: If place_k: append top_card to row_k, then draw one card at random from deck into top_card and remove it from deck.

If take_k: for each card in row_k, add 1 to the active player's matching red/blue/green/yellow/purple, or to plus2 for a '+2' card. Then set row_k to empty, append k to closed_rows, and set the active player's taken = true.

When every player's taken = true: set every taken = false, empty row_1, row_2, row_3 and closed_rows, add 1 to cycle, and leave active_seat unchanged (the last taker starts). Otherwise: set active_seat to the first seat in order s+1, s+2, s (wrapping 3 to 1) whose taken = false.

When cycle == 4: set favourite_shown = favourite for each player. With T(c) = c*(c+1)/2, F = the count of the player's favourite colour and o1..o4 = the other four counts, set score = T(F) + 2*max(T(o1),T(o2),T(o3),T(o4)) - (T(o1)+T(o2)+T(o3)+T(o4)) + 2*plus2.
When cycle == 4: announce every player's favourite_shown and score.
End the game if cycle == 4; otherwise continue.

ending.decided_by: Each player's standing is their final score from the formula (Favourite colour plus the single largest other colour score positive, the other three colours score negative, and each +2 card adds 2). The highest score wins; players tied at the top share the result, which the source calls a draw.

rules.text: At setup, the deck holds 38 cards (7 each of Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple and 3 '+2'), one is turned up as top_card leaving 37 in deck, all rows and closed_rows are empty, cycle = 1 and active_seat = 1.
At setup, each of the 3 players is dealt a different Favourite from the 5 colours, visible only to its owner, and the 2 undealt colours are never revealed.
Tableau counts (red, blue, green, yellow, purple, plus2) are public throughout the game.
Only the player at active_seat is asked to act on a turn.
When row k is not in closed_rows and holds fewer than 3 cards, then place_k is offered; otherwise it is not.
When row k is not in closed_rows and holds at least 1 card, then take_k is offered; otherwise it is not.
When the active player chooses place_k, then top_card is appended to row_k and a new top_card is drawn from deck, reducing deck by 1.

When the active player chooses take_k, then each card in row_k adds 1 to that player's matching colour count (or plus2 for a '+2'), row_k becomes empty, k is appended to closed_rows and the player's taken = true.
When all 3 players have taken = true, then every taken resets to false, all rows and closed_rows are emptied, cycle increases by 1, and active_seat stays the player who just took.
When the cycle does not end, then active_seat becomes the first seat among s+1, s+2, s (wrapping 1-2-3) with taken = false, which may be the same player.
When only one player has not taken and their open row is full, then their only option is to take that row.
When cycle reaches 4 (after 3 cycles), then the game ends.
At game end, every player's Favourite is announced publicly.
At game end, score = T(F) + 2*max(T(o1..o4)) - sum(T(o1..o4)) + 2*plus2, where T(c) = c(c+1)/2; for example favourite 4, others 3,1,0,0 and plus2 1 gives 10 + 6 - 7 + 2 = 11.
When two other colours tie for the largest count, then only one of them scores positive and the other scores negative.
The player with the highest score wins, and players tied for the highest score share the top (a draw).

offers.question: Active player's action
offers.options: place_k for each row k not in closed_rows with fewer than 3 cards, plus take_k for each row k not in closed_rows with at least 1 card. When all open rows are full, only take options. At the start of a cycle (all rows empty), only place_1, place_2, place_3. Seats other than active_seat are offered nothing.

choices.why: The designer fixed the table at 3, and the rules tie the 3 rows and 3 distinct Favourites to 3 players, so the minimum and maximum are both 3.
The rules state there is no table talk. The strategy is in reading which colours rivals take, guessing their hidden Favourites, and placing cards that hurt them while hiding your own.

choices.what: favourite_pool table list and favourite_shown attribute
choices.why: These give the dealing of distinct Favourites and the end-of-game reveal a concrete piece of state to act on.

choices.what: Score computed only at game end
choices.why: The rules say scoring happens once, at game end.

simplifications.what: One engine round is one player's turn, with the active seat tracked in active_seat
simplifications.why: The engine runs a flat step list. Turn order, including the same player acting again, is handled by arithmetic on taken.

simplifications.what: A tie for the highest score is shown as a shared win
simplifications.why: The engine has no separate draw; players level at the top share the win, which corresponds to the source's draw.

simplifications.what: Shuffling is done as random draws from the deck list
simplifications.why: The engine draws at random from a list.
